verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The exiles have eyes but do not see (v. 2), so Ezekiel is told to act it out: pack an exile's bag by day, dig through the wall at dusk and carry it out on his shoulder with his face covered (vv. 3-6). He does exactly that (v. 7). Next morning he explains: I am a sign for you: as I have done, so shall it be done to them (vv. 8-11). The prince in Jerusalem will flee through a hole in the wall at dusk; God will catch him in his net and bring him to Babylon, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there (vv. 12-13). His troops will be scattered, and a few survivors will confess their abominations among the nations (vv. 14-16).
verseByVerse.theology: God's word was fulfilled to the smallest detail in the fall of Jerusalem's king.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a rebellious house, who have eyes to see, but see not, who have ears to hear, but hear not, for they are a rebellious house.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a rebellious house, who have eyes to see, but see not, who have ears to hear, but hear not, for they are a rebellious house.

The problem is not lack of information. The exiles had eyes and ears. They had watched Ezekiel's brick and his hair and heard his warnings for more than a year. They see not because they will not.

Isaiah had been told his hearers would be like this (Isa 6:9-10), and Jesus said the same about the crowds of his day: seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand (Matt 13:13). He even said it to his own disciples: Having eyes do you not see, and having ears do you not hear? (Mark 8:18). Spiritual blindness is a condition of the heart, not the eyes. Only God can open them.

verseByVerse.quote: As for you, son of man, prepare for yourself an exile's baggage, and go into exile by day in their sight. You shall go like an exile from your place to another place in their sight. Perhaps they will understand, though they are a rebellious house. You shall bring out your baggage by day in their sight, as baggage for exile, and you shall go out yourself at evening in their sight, as those do who must go into exile. In their sight dig through the wall, and bring your baggage out through it. In their sight you shall lift the baggage upon your shoulder and carry it out at dusk. You shall cover your face that you may not see the land, for I have made you a sign for the house of Israel."
verseByVerse.commentary:
As for you, son of man, prepare for yourself an exile's baggage, and go into exile by day in their sight. You shall go like an exile from your place to another place in their sight. Perhaps they will understand, though they are a rebellious house.

Picture a refugee's bundle: a blanket, a water skin, a little food, whatever can be carried on one shoulder. Ezekiel packs one in broad daylight, where everyone can watch.

And listen to God's heart: Perhaps they will understand. (The ESV notes this may be read "will see that".) Even with a rebellious house, God keeps trying. He does not give up on people easily.

You shall bring out your baggage by day in their sight, as baggage for exile, and you shall go out yourself at evening in their sight, as those do who must go into exile.

In their sight dig through the wall, and bring your baggage out through it.

In their sight you shall lift the baggage upon your shoulder and carry it out at dusk. You shall cover your face that you may not see the land, for I have made you a sign for the house of Israel."

Seven times in these verses: in their sight. The whole performance is for them. Digging through a mud-brick wall at dusk is what someone does who cannot leave by the gate — a fugitive, sneaking out. And the covered face says: you will never see this land again.

The exiles in Babylon were hoping for a quick return. Ezekiel is showing them a second exile still to come, from Jerusalem itself.

verseByVerse.quote: And I did as I was commanded. I brought out my baggage by day, as baggage for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my own hands. I brought out my baggage at dusk, carrying it on my shoulder in their sight. In the morning the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said to you, 'What are you doing?' Say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: This oracle concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are in it.' Say, 'I am a sign for you: as I have done, so shall it be done to them. They shall go into exile, into captivity.'
verseByVerse.commentary:
And I did as I was commanded. I brought out my baggage by day, as baggage for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my own hands. I brought out my baggage at dusk, carrying it on my shoulder in their sight.

I did as I was commanded. Simple, complete obedience, however strange the instruction. Ezekiel dug through his own house with his bare hands.

And notice when the explanation came: In the morning (v. 8). Ezekiel packed, dug and carried his bundle without being told what it meant. He obeyed first and understood afterward. That is often how God leads his people. Jesus said to Peter, What I am doing you do not understand now, but afterward you will understand (John 13:7).

In the morning the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said to you, 'What are you doing?'

The sign worked in one way: it made people ask. What are you doing? That question is an opening. Faithful witness often looks strange enough to make people curious.

Say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: This oracle concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are in it.'

Say, 'I am a sign for you: as I have done, so shall it be done to them. They shall go into exile, into captivity.'

The ESV notes that This oracle concerns may be rendered "This burden is". The prophet's own body has become the message: I am a sign for you. Ezekiel's life was not his own. It was a sermon God preached through him.

verseByVerse.quote: And the prince who is among them shall lift his baggage upon his shoulder at dusk, and shall go out. They shall dig through the wall to bring him out through it. He shall cover his face, that he may not see the land with his eyes. And I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my snare. And I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there. And I will scatter toward every wind all who are around him, his helpers and all his troops, and I will unsheathe the sword after them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the prince who is among them shall lift his baggage upon his shoulder at dusk, and shall go out. They shall dig through the wall to bring him out through it. He shall cover his face, that he may not see the land with his eyes.

And I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my snare. And I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there.

Now the sign is decoded, and it is astonishingly precise. The prince is Zedekiah, king in Jerusalem. About six years later, when the Babylonians broke into the city, all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls (2 Kgs 25:4). The king ran in the dark.

And then the riddle: I will bring him to Babylon... yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there. How could a man be taken to Babylon and not see it? Here is how. The Babylonians caught Zedekiah, put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him in chains, and the king of Babylon took him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death (Jer 52:11). He went to Babylon blind. He never saw it. He died there.

Notice who catches him: I will spread my net over him. Babylon's soldiers did the chasing, but it was God's net. No one outruns the word of God.

And I will scatter toward every wind all who are around him, his helpers and all his troops, and I will unsheathe the sword after them.

And so it happened: all his army was scattered from him (2 Kgs 25:5). The men who were supposed to protect the king ran for their lives.

verseByVerse.quote: And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them among the countries. But I will let a few of them escape from the sword, from famine and pestilence, that they may declare all their abominations among the nations where they go, and may know that I am the LORD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them among the countries.

But I will let a few of them escape from the sword, from famine and pestilence, that they may declare all their abominations among the nations where they go, and may know that I am the LORD."

Why spare a few? Not because they deserve it, but so that they may declare all their abominations among the nations. The survivors will be living testimony. Wherever they go, they will have to explain why Jerusalem fell: not because Babylon's gods were stronger, but because Judah sinned and the LORD judged.

That is a strange but real kind of witness — confessing sin. The nations would learn about the holiness of Israel's God from the lips of people who had broken his law. God's glory is displayed even in the honest confession of those he disciplines.

Christians too are called sojourners and exiles (1 Pet 2:11), with no lasting city here (Heb 13:14). Part of our witness in the world is being honest about our sin and pointing to the grace that forgives it.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel must eat his bread trembling and drink his water anxiously (v. 18), as a sign that Jerusalem's people will eat in fear because the land will be stripped for the violence done in it (v. 19). The cities will be laid waste, and you shall know that I am the LORD (v. 20).
verseByVerse.theology: Violence against others brings the loss of every security.

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, eat your bread with quaking, and drink water with trembling and with anxiety. And say to the people of the land, Thus says the Lord GOD concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread with anxiety, and drink water in dismay. In this way her land will be stripped of all it contains, on account of the violence of all those who dwell in it. And the inhabited cities shall be laid waste, and the land shall become a desolation; and you shall know that I am the LORD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, eat your bread with quaking, and drink water with trembling and with anxiety.

Another sign, this time at the table. Ezekiel eats with shaking hands, as if every meal might be the last, like someone eating during an air raid.

And say to the people of the land, Thus says the Lord GOD concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread with anxiety, and drink water in dismay. In this way her land will be stripped of all it contains, on account of the violence of all those who dwell in it.

The reason is stated plainly: on account of the violence of all those who dwell in it. Jerusalem's people had made others live in fear through oppression and bloodshed. Now they will live in fear themselves. What we do to others has a way of coming back to us.

And the inhabited cities shall be laid waste, and the land shall become a desolation; and you shall know that I am the LORD."

A table where people eat in peace is one of God's quiet gifts. Many believers across the world today eat their bread with anxiety because of persecution or war. Pray for them. And give thanks when you can eat without fear.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 21–28 — None of My Words Will Be Delayed
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The people have a proverb: The days grow long, and every vision comes to nothing (v. 22). God will end it: The days are near, and the fulfillment of every vision (vv. 23-24). I will speak the word and perform it (v. 25). Others say the prophet's visions are for many days from now (vv. 26-27), but God answers, None of my words will be delayed any longer (v. 28).
verseByVerse.theology: Delay is not denial; God's word will be done in his time, and that time is closer than scoffers think.

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, what is this proverb that you have about the land of Israel, saying, 'The days grow long, and every vision comes to nothing'? Tell them therefore, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel.' But say to them, The days are near, and the fulfillment of every vision. For there shall be no more any false vision or flattering divination within the house of Israel. For I am the LORD; I will speak the word that I will speak, and it will be performed. It will no longer be delayed, but in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak the word and perform it, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, what is this proverb that you have about the land of Israel, saying, 'The days grow long, and every vision comes to nothing'?

The people had a saying, and the ESV notes that the you is plural: everyone was saying it. The days grow long, and every vision comes to nothing. In other words: the prophets have been warning for years, and nothing has happened. It is all talk.

This is an old and dangerous form of unbelief. It does not argue against God's word; it just waits it out. Peter heard the same in his day: Where is the promise of his coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, all things are continuing as they were (2 Pet 3:4).

Tell them therefore, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel.' But say to them, The days are near, and the fulfillment of every vision.

God rewrites the proverb. Not every vision comes to nothing, but The days are near, and the fulfillment of every vision. (The ESV notes that fulfillment is literally "word": every vision's word is about to come true.)

For there shall be no more any false vision or flattering divination within the house of Israel.

Flattering divination — prophecy that tells people pleasant things about themselves. When God's word is fulfilled, the flatterers will be silenced, because events will expose them. Flattery always feels kind and always does harm: a flattering mouth works ruin (Prov 26:28). Be wary of any voice, in the pulpit or in your own head, that only ever tells you how well you are doing.

For I am the LORD; I will speak the word that I will speak, and it will be performed. It will no longer be delayed, but in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak the word and perform it, declares the Lord GOD."

I will speak the word... and it will be performed. That is the difference between God's word and every other voice. It shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose (Isa 55:11). The delay was patience, not weakness. If it seems slow, wait for it; it will surely come (Hab 2:3).

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, behold, they of the house of Israel say, 'The vision that he sees is for many days from now, and he prophesies of times far off.' Therefore say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: None of my words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, behold, they of the house of Israel say, 'The vision that he sees is for many days from now, and he prophesies of times far off.'

This is a subtler unbelief. These people do not say the visions are false. They say: they are true, but they are about the distant future. Not us. Not now.

That is exactly how many people treat God's warnings today. Judgment, death, the return of Christ — yes, perhaps, some day. But far off. Not something to act on this week.

Therefore say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: None of my words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed, declares the Lord GOD."

Within a few years, Jerusalem fell. The "far-off" vision arrived in their own lifetime.

The lesson is not to calculate dates but to live ready. Behold, now is the favorable time; behold, now is the day of salvation (2 Cor 6:2). The word God has spoken about the end will be performed, and The Lord is not slow to fulfill his promise as some count slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish (2 Pet 3:9). Do not mistake his patience for a postponement you can use to put off repentance.

12.title: Baggage for Exile
12.overview:
Ezekiel lives among people who have eyes but do not see. God tells him to act out exile: to pack an exile's baggage by day in their sight, dig through the wall at dusk, and carry the baggage out on his shoulder with his face covered. He obeys. The next morning, when they ask what he is doing, he explains that he is a sign: the prince in Jerusalem will flee through the wall at dusk with his face covered; God will catch him in his net and bring him to Babylon, yet he will not see it and will die there. His troops will be scattered, and a few survivors will declare their abominations among the nations (vv. 1-16).

Ezekiel is to eat his bread with quaking and drink with trembling, as a sign that Jerusalem's people will eat in anxiety while their land is stripped because of their violence (vv. 17-20).

God ends the popular proverb that the days go on and every vision comes to nothing: the days are near, and every vision will be fulfilled. He also answers those who say the visions concern the distant future: none of his words will be delayed any longer; what he speaks will be done (vv. 21-28).
12.theology:
Spiritual blindness is a matter of the will and the heart, and God graciously keeps offering signs (vv. 2-3; Isa 6:9-10; Matt 13:13).

God's word is fulfilled in precise detail: the blinded king taken to Babylon who never saw it (vv. 12-13; 2 Kgs 25:4-7; Jer 52:11).

God can make even the confession of disciplined sinners a witness to the nations (v. 16).

Violence against others brings its own fear and loss (v. 19).

The delay of judgment is patience, not weakness, and God's word will not return empty (vv. 22-28; Isa 55:11; Hab 2:3; 2 Pet 3:4, 9).

Treating God's warnings as far off is a dangerous form of unbelief; now is the day of salvation (vv. 27-28; 2 Cor 6:2).
12.examples:
A refugee's bundle packed in broad daylight.

A priest digging through his own wall with his hands.

A king taken to Babylon who never saw Babylon.

Eating dinner with shaking hands.

A proverb that said: it is all talk.

True, but not for us, not now.

13.text: <sup>1</sup>The word of the LORD came to me:<sup>2</sup>"Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel, who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy from their own hearts: 'Hear the word of the LORD!'<sup>3</sup>Thus says the Lord GOD, Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!<sup>4</sup>Your prophets have been like jackals among ruins, O Israel.<sup>5</sup>You have not gone up into the breaches, or built up a wall for the house of Israel, that it might stand in battle in the day of the LORD.<sup>6</sup>They have seen false visions and lying divinations. They say, 'Declares the LORD,' when the LORD has not sent them, and yet they expect him to fulfill their word.<sup>7</sup>Have you not seen a false vision and uttered a lying divination, whenever you have said, 'Declares the LORD,' although I have not spoken?"<sup>8</sup>Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "Because you have uttered falsehood and seen lying visions, therefore behold, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD.<sup>9</sup>My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and who give lying divinations. They shall not be in the council of my people, nor be enrolled in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord GOD.<sup>10</sup>Precisely because they have misled my people, saying, 'Peace,' when there is no peace, and because, when the people build a wall, these prophets smear it with whitewash,<sup>11</sup>say to those who smear it with whitewash that it shall fall! There will be a deluge of rain, and you, O great hailstones, will fall, and a stormy wind break out.<sup>12</sup>And when the wall falls, will it not be said to you, 'Where is the coating with which you smeared it?'<sup>13</sup>Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will make a stormy wind break out in my wrath, and there shall be a deluge of rain in my anger, and great hailstones in wrath to make a full end.<sup>14</sup>And I will break down the wall that you have smeared with whitewash, and bring it down to the ground, so that its foundation will be laid bare. When it falls, you shall perish in the midst of it, and you shall know that I am the LORD.<sup>15</sup>Thus will I spend my wrath upon the wall and upon those who have smeared it with whitewash, and I will say to you, The wall is no more, nor those who smeared it,<sup>16</sup>the prophets of Israel who prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her, when there was no peace, declares the Lord GOD.<sup>17</sup>"And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people, who prophesy out of their own hearts. Prophesy against them<sup>18</sup>and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the women who sew magic bands upon all wrists, and make veils for the heads of persons of every stature, in the hunt for souls! Will you hunt down souls belonging to my people and keep your own souls alive?<sup>19</sup>You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, putting to death souls who should not die and keeping alive souls who should not live, by your lying to my people, who listen to lies.<sup>20</sup>"Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against your magic bands with which you hunt the souls like birds, and I will tear them from your arms, and I will let the souls whom you hunt go free, the souls like birds.<sup>21</sup>Your veils also I will tear off and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand as prey, and you shall know that I am the LORD.<sup>22</sup>Because you have disheartened the righteous falsely, although I have not grieved him, and you have encouraged the wicked, that he should not turn from his evil way to save his life,<sup>23</sup>therefore you shall no more see false visions nor practice divination. I will deliver my people out of your hand. And you shall know that I am the LORD."

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel prophesies against those who prophesy from their own hearts (v. 2), foolish prophets who have seen nothing (v. 3). They are like jackals in ruins (v. 4); they have not stood in the breach (v. 5); they say Declares the LORD when he has not sent them (vv. 6-7). God is against them, and they will be shut out of his people (vv. 8-9). They cried Peace when there was no peace, and when the people built a flimsy wall, they covered it with whitewash (v. 10). God will send storm, rain and hail to bring it down, and the prophets will perish with it (vv. 11-16).
verseByVerse.theology: Preachers who cover sin with comforting words instead of exposing it will fall with the wall they whitewashed.

verseByVerse.quote: The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel, who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy from their own hearts: 'Hear the word of the LORD!' Thus says the Lord GOD, Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!
verseByVerse.commentary:
The word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel, who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy from their own hearts: 'Hear the word of the LORD!'

Ezekiel was not the only prophet in town. There were plenty of others, and they were far more popular. The difference is one phrase: they prophesy from their own hearts. Their messages came from their own imagination, hopes and ambitions.

Jeremiah was fighting the same prophets in Jerusalem: They speak visions of their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD (Jer 23:16). And Peter describes the opposite: no prophecy was ever produced by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit (2 Pet 1:21). The test of any preacher is not how moving he is, but whether his message comes from God's word or from his own heart.

Thus says the Lord GOD, Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!

Follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing. They talked about visions, but there was nothing behind the talk. Confident, eloquent and empty.

verseByVerse.quote: Your prophets have been like jackals among ruins, O Israel. You have not gone up into the breaches, or built up a wall for the house of Israel, that it might stand in battle in the day of the LORD. They have seen false visions and lying divinations. They say, 'Declares the LORD,' when the LORD has not sent them, and yet they expect him to fulfill their word. Have you not seen a false vision and uttered a lying divination, whenever you have said, 'Declares the LORD,' although I have not spoken?"
verseByVerse.commentary:
Your prophets have been like jackals among ruins, O Israel.

Jackals scavenge in ruins. They do not rebuild anything; they feed on the wreckage. So these prophets profited from a collapsing nation — gaining followers, influence and income while the country fell apart.

You have not gone up into the breaches, or built up a wall for the house of Israel, that it might stand in battle in the day of the LORD.

A true prophet stands in the gap in the wall where the enemy breaks through. He calls people to repentance, which is the only real defence on the day of the LORD. God will later say he searched for such a man and found none (22:30). The false prophets never went near the breach. It was dangerous and unpopular. They stayed where it was comfortable.

They have seen false visions and lying divinations. They say, 'Declares the LORD,' when the LORD has not sent them, and yet they expect him to fulfill their word.

Have you not seen a false vision and uttered a lying divination, whenever you have said, 'Declares the LORD,' although I have not spoken?"

They borrowed God's name for their own words. And they believed it themselves — they expect him to fulfill their word. Self-deceived deceivers are especially persuasive.

Moses had given the test: when a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD, if the word does not come to pass or come true, that is a word that the LORD has not spoken (Deut 18:22). It is a grave thing to put "God told me" in front of your own ideas.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "Because you have uttered falsehood and seen lying visions, therefore behold, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD. My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and who give lying divinations. They shall not be in the council of my people, nor be enrolled in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "Because you have uttered falsehood and seen lying visions, therefore behold, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD.

My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and who give lying divinations. They shall not be in the council of my people, nor be enrolled in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord GOD.

Three exclusions, each worse than the last. They will lose their seat in the council of God's people. Their names will not be written in the register of Israel — the list of those who belong. And they will never return to the land.

The register reminds us of something greater. Jesus told his disciples not to rejoice in spiritual power, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven (Luke 10:20). It is possible to speak in God's name, draw crowds and still not be written in God's book. What matters is not whether we speak about God, but whether God knows us.

verseByVerse.quote: Precisely because they have misled my people, saying, 'Peace,' when there is no peace, and because, when the people build a wall, these prophets smear it with whitewash, say to those who smear it with whitewash that it shall fall! There will be a deluge of rain, and you, O great hailstones, will fall, and a stormy wind break out. And when the wall falls, will it not be said to you, 'Where is the coating with which you smeared it?'
verseByVerse.commentary:
Precisely because they have misled my people, saying, 'Peace,' when there is no peace, and because, when the people build a wall, these prophets smear it with whitewash,

Here is the heart of their error: saying, 'Peace,' when there is no peace. Jeremiah had used almost the same words (Jer 6:14). The nation was under God's judgment, and the prophets said everything was fine.

Then a vivid picture. The people build a flimsy wall — their own plans for security, their alliances, their hopes. It is badly built and will not stand. The prophets come along and smear it with whitewash (the ESV notes, "plaster"). Now it looks solid. The cracks are covered. But nothing has actually been fixed.

That is exactly what false comfort does. It paints over sin instead of dealing with it. Jesus called religious leaders whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead people's bones (Matt 23:27). And Paul, struck on the high priest's orders, called him you whitewashed wall! (Acts 23:3).

say to those who smear it with whitewash that it shall fall! There will be a deluge of rain, and you, O great hailstones, will fall, and a stormy wind break out.

And when the wall falls, will it not be said to you, 'Where is the coating with which you smeared it?'

Whitewash cannot stop a storm. When the rain and hail and wind come, the wall falls, and people will turn to the prophets and ask: where is your plaster now? Where are your reassurances?

Notice that God speaks to the weather itself: you, O great hailstones, will fall. The storm is not blind nature. Wind and hail are his servants — fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind fulfilling his word! (Ps 148:8). The same creation the false prophets ignored will carry out God's verdict on their work.

Jesus told the same story about two houses. The rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell, and great was the fall of it (Matt 7:27). The only thing that stands in the storm is what is built on the rock of his word, heard and obeyed.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will make a stormy wind break out in my wrath, and there shall be a deluge of rain in my anger, and great hailstones in wrath to make a full end. And I will break down the wall that you have smeared with whitewash, and bring it down to the ground, so that its foundation will be laid bare. When it falls, you shall perish in the midst of it, and you shall know that I am the LORD. Thus will I spend my wrath upon the wall and upon those who have smeared it with whitewash, and I will say to you, The wall is no more, nor those who smeared it, the prophets of Israel who prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her, when there was no peace, declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will make a stormy wind break out in my wrath, and there shall be a deluge of rain in my anger, and great hailstones in wrath to make a full end.

And I will break down the wall that you have smeared with whitewash, and bring it down to the ground, so that its foundation will be laid bare. When it falls, you shall perish in the midst of it, and you shall know that I am the LORD.

The storm is God's own: in my wrath... in my anger. And when the wall comes down, even its foundation will be laid bare. Everything false will be exposed to the bottom. And the prophets who whitewashed it will be crushed under it.

Thus will I spend my wrath upon the wall and upon those who have smeared it with whitewash, and I will say to you, The wall is no more, nor those who smeared it,

the prophets of Israel who prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her, when there was no peace, declares the Lord GOD.

The wall is no more, nor those who smeared it. Both the false security and the false preachers disappear together.

This is a searching word for every pastor, and for every church that wants to hear only good news. The most loving thing a preacher can do is tell the truth about sin, so that people can find real peace — the peace that comes not from whitewash but from the cross. Soothing words that leave people unrepentant are not kindness. They are cruelty dressed as compassion.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel turns against the women who prophesy out of their own hearts, sewing magic bands and making veils in the hunt for souls (vv. 17-18). For handfuls of barley and bread they have pronounced death on those who should live and life on those who should die (v. 19). God will tear off their bands and veils and set his people free like birds from a trap (vv. 20-21), Because you have disheartened the righteous falsely... and you have encouraged the wicked (vv. 22-23).
verseByVerse.theology: False spirituality preys on people for gain, discourages the righteous and comforts the wicked; God rescues his people from it.

verseByVerse.quote: "And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people, who prophesy out of their own hearts. Prophesy against them and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the women who sew magic bands upon all wrists, and make veils for the heads of persons of every stature, in the hunt for souls! Will you hunt down souls belonging to my people and keep your own souls alive? You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, putting to death souls who should not die and keeping alive souls who should not live, by your lying to my people, who listen to lies.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people, who prophesy out of their own hearts. Prophesy against them

Now a second group: women who also prophesy out of their own hearts. The problem is not that they are women — Scripture honours true prophetesses like Deborah and Huldah (Judg 4:4; 2 Kgs 22:14) — but that their message, like the men's, is their own invention.

and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the women who sew magic bands upon all wrists, and make veils for the heads of persons of every stature, in the hunt for souls! Will you hunt down souls belonging to my people and keep your own souls alive?

These are occult practices: bands tied on the wrists, veils put over people's heads, rituals sold as spiritual power. And God calls it what it is: the hunt for souls. They trap people like a hunter traps birds.

And look at the question God asks: Will you hunt down souls belonging to my people and keep your own souls alive? These women were feeding themselves by feeding on others. Their own survival came at the cost of the people they claimed to help. That is the mark of every false shepherd: the flock exists for them, not they for the flock.

You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, putting to death souls who should not die and keeping alive souls who should not live, by your lying to my people, who listen to lies.

And they do it for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread — for payment, even small payment. False spirituality has always been a business. People pay to be told what they want to hear, or to buy protection from what they fear.

And God names the deepest wrong: You have profaned me among my people. They took God's holy name and used it as a tool to make a living. Paul warned against people imagining that godliness is a means of gain (1 Tim 6:5). When religion becomes a business, it is not only people who are harmed; God himself is dishonoured.

Worse, they pronounce life and death falsely: putting to death souls who should not die and keeping alive souls who should not live. They terrified the innocent and reassured the guilty. And the people went along because they listen to lies. There is always a market for spiritual falsehood where people prefer comfort to truth.

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against your magic bands with which you hunt the souls like birds, and I will tear them from your arms, and I will let the souls whom you hunt go free, the souls like birds. Your veils also I will tear off and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand as prey, and you shall know that I am the LORD. Because you have disheartened the righteous falsely, although I have not grieved him, and you have encouraged the wicked, that he should not turn from his evil way to save his life, therefore you shall no more see false visions nor practice divination. I will deliver my people out of your hand. And you shall know that I am the LORD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against your magic bands with which you hunt the souls like birds, and I will tear them from your arms, and I will let the souls whom you hunt go free, the souls like birds.

Your veils also I will tear off and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand as prey, and you shall know that I am the LORD.

Here is the good news in the middle of the judgment. God will rip off the bands and the veils and let the souls whom you hunt go free, the souls like birds. His people are not left in the trap. We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped! (Ps 124:7).

Jesus contrasted himself with every such hunter: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I came that they may have life and have it abundantly. I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:10-11). False teachers take from the sheep; the true Shepherd gives himself for them.

Because you have disheartened the righteous falsely, although I have not grieved him, and you have encouraged the wicked, that he should not turn from his evil way to save his life,

This verse is a perfect summary of false teaching in every age. It does two things. It disheartened the righteous falsely — loading guilt and fear on people God was not grieving over. And it encouraged the wicked — telling people living in sin that they had nothing to fear, that he should not turn from his evil way to save his life.

True preaching does the opposite. It comforts the broken-hearted and warns the complacent. Woe to those who call evil good and good evil (Isa 5:20). The false prophets of Jerusalem strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns from his evil (Jer 23:14). Ask of any teaching you listen to: does it lead the guilty to repentance and the repentant to peace?

therefore you shall no more see false visions nor practice divination. I will deliver my people out of your hand. And you shall know that I am the LORD."

The chapter ends with God's promise to his people: I will deliver my people out of your hand. God does not leave his flock to wolves forever. He exposes false teachers and rescues those they have trapped.

13.title: Whitewash on a Crumbling Wall
13.overview:
God tells Ezekiel to prophesy against the prophets of Israel who speak from their own hearts and have seen nothing. They are like jackals among ruins; they have not stood in the breaches or built up the wall for the day of the LORD. They claim God's authority when he has not sent them. God is against them: they will be excluded from the council and register of his people and will not enter the land. Because they have said peace when there is no peace and have covered the people's flimsy wall with whitewash, God will send storm, rain and hail to bring the wall down to its foundations, and the prophets will perish with it (vv. 1-16).

Ezekiel then prophesies against women who also prophesy from their own hearts, using magic bands and veils to hunt souls for handfuls of barley and pieces of bread, condemning those who should live and sparing those who should die. God will tear away their bands and veils and set his people free like birds. Because they have discouraged the righteous and encouraged the wicked not to turn from evil, they will see no more false visions, and God will deliver his people from them (vv. 17-23).
13.theology:
A true message comes from God, not from the preacher's own heart; claiming God's authority for one's own words is grave sin (vv. 2-3, 6-7; Jer 23:16; 2 Pet 1:20-21; Deut 18:20-22).

Faithful ministry stands in the breach and calls people to repentance before the day of the LORD (v. 5; 22:30).

Speaking about God is not the same as being known by God (v. 9; Luke 10:20).

False peace whitewashes sin instead of dealing with it, and it will not survive God's storm (vv. 10-16; Jer 6:14; Matt 7:24-27; 23:27).

False spirituality preys on people for gain, discourages the righteous and encourages the wicked (vv. 18-22; Isa 5:20; Jer 23:14).

God rescues his people from false teachers; Christ the good shepherd gives life where the thief takes it (vv. 20-23; Ps 124:7; John 10:10-11).
13.examples:
Jackals growing fat in the ruins.

Nobody standing in the gap in the wall.

A fresh coat of whitewash on a wall that is already cracking.

Where is your plaster now?

Spiritual advice sold for a handful of barley.

A snare torn open and the birds flying free.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Elders come to consult Ezekiel (v. 1), but God sees what they carry: these men have taken their idols into their hearts — should he let himself be consulted by them? (vv. 2-3). Anyone who comes to the prophet with idols in his heart, God will answer himself, to lay hold of hearts estranged from him (vv. 4-5). Repent and turn away from your idols (v. 6). Whoever comes with idols in the heart will face God's opposition and be cut off (vv. 7-8); a prophet who goes along will share the guilt (vv. 9-10), so that Israel will no longer stray, but that they may be my people and I may be their God (v. 11).
verseByVerse.theology: God will not be used by people who keep their idols; he confronts them in order to win back their hearts.

verseByVerse.quote: Then certain of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me. And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their hearts, and set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces. Should I indeed let myself be consulted by them?
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then certain of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.

The elders come again to Ezekiel's house (as in 8:1). Outwardly it looks good: leaders seeking a word from God.

And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their hearts, and set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces. Should I indeed let myself be consulted by them?

God sees what Ezekiel cannot: these men have taken their idols into their hearts. There may have been no statues in their homes in Babylon. The idols had moved inside.

This is a deep insight into sin. Idolatry is not first about carved images. It is about what the heart loves, trusts and serves in place of God. The New Testament calls greed idolatry: covetousness, which is idolatry (Col 3:5). And its last word to believers is Little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). Anything we look to for the security, meaning or joy that only God can give is an idol — money, approval, success, a relationship, comfort, control.

And they have set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces. They keep it right in front of them, where it trips them every day, and they still come to church, as it were, to ask God for guidance. Should I indeed let myself be consulted by them? God will not be a consultant to people who have no intention of giving up their idols.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore speak to them and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Any one of the house of Israel who takes his idols into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and yet comes to the prophet, I the LORD will answer him as he comes with the multitude of his idols, that I may lay hold of the hearts of the house of Israel, who are all estranged from me through their idols.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore speak to them and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: Any one of the house of Israel who takes his idols into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and yet comes to the prophet, I the LORD will answer him as he comes with the multitude of his idols,

I the LORD will answer him as he comes with the multitude of his idols. Not the answer he wants, but an answer that fits what he is carrying. God deals with the heart that comes, not the words it says.

that I may lay hold of the hearts of the house of Israel, who are all estranged from me through their idols.

And here is the purpose, full of grace: that I may lay hold of the hearts. God confronts them not to push them away but to grab hold of them. Their hearts had drifted, estranged from me. He wants them back.

That is why God sometimes refuses to give us the easy answer we pray for. He is after our hearts, not just our requests.

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: Repent and turn away from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your abominations. For any one of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who sojourn in Israel, who separates himself from me, taking his idols into his heart and putting the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and yet comes to a prophet to consult me through him, I the LORD will answer him myself. And I will set my face against that man; I will make him a sign and a byword and cut him off from the midst of my people, and you shall know that I am the LORD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: Repent and turn away from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your abominations.

The call is simple and total: Repent and turn away. Not merely feel sorry. Turn — first from the idols, then the face from the abominations. Repentance is a change of direction, a change of what you are looking at.

For any one of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who sojourn in Israel, who separates himself from me, taking his idols into his heart and putting the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and yet comes to a prophet to consult me through him, I the LORD will answer him myself.

The same rule applies to native Israelites and to foreigners living among them. God has no double standard. And notice the phrase who separates himself from me. Idolatry is not a small addition to faith; it is a separation from God.

And I will set my face against that man; I will make him a sign and a byword and cut him off from the midst of my people, and you shall know that I am the LORD.

I the LORD will answer him myself — and the answer is to set my face against that man. It is a fearful thing to come to God with a divided heart and find that God himself answers.

Jesus quoted Isaiah about people like this: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; in vain do they worship me (Matt 15:8-9). Religious activity without a heart turned from idols is not neutral. It is in vain.

verseByVerse.quote: And if the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, the LORD, have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand against him and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel. And they shall bear their punishment —the punishment of the prophet and the punishment of the inquirer shall be alike— that the house of Israel may no more go astray from me, nor defile themselves anymore with all their transgressions, but that they may be my people and I may be their God, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And if the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, the LORD, have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand against him and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel.

This is a hard verse, and it should be read carefully. It does not mean God lies or tempts anyone to lie. God never lies (Titus 1:2). It means that when people insist on hearing falsehood, God may hand them over to it. A prophet willing to tell idol-worshippers what they want to hear will be allowed to do so — and both will fall together.

Scripture shows this pattern elsewhere. When King Ahab wanted only prophets who agreed with him, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these your prophets (1 Kgs 22:23). And Paul says of those who refused to love the truth and so be saved: Therefore God sends them a strong delusion, so that they may believe what is false (2 Thess 2:10-11). This is God's judgment on people who have already chosen lies. The best protection is to love the truth, even when it hurts.

And they shall bear their punishment —the punishment of the prophet and the punishment of the inquirer shall be alike—

The ESV notes that punishment may be "iniquity", three times in this verse. The false prophet and the one who seeks him out share the same guilt. The one who asks for a lie is as responsible as the one who tells it.

that the house of Israel may no more go astray from me, nor defile themselves anymore with all their transgressions, but that they may be my people and I may be their God, declares the Lord GOD."

And again the purpose is restoration. The goal of all this severity is the covenant promise: that they may be my people and I may be their God. God's discipline always aims at a relationship.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: When a land sins against God and he sends famine, wild beasts, sword or pestilence (vv. 13, 15, 17, 19), even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver but their own lives by their righteousness (vv. 14, 20) — not even their own sons and daughters (vv. 16, 18). How much more when God sends all four judgments on Jerusalem! (v. 21). Yet survivors will come out, and when the exiles see their ways, they will be consoled, knowing that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it (vv. 22-23).
verseByVerse.theology: No human righteousness can rescue another person; only the righteousness of Christ counts for others.

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, when a land sins against me by acting faithlessly, and I stretch out my hand against it and break its supply of bread and send famine upon it, and cut off from it man and beast, even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver but their own lives by their righteousness, declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, when a land sins against me by acting faithlessly, and I stretch out my hand against it and break its supply of bread and send famine upon it, and cut off from it man and beast,

A new message answers a quiet hope. Perhaps some exiles thought: surely God will spare Jerusalem because of the righteous people still living there. Abraham had once pleaded for Sodom for the sake of ten righteous (Gen 18:32). (Once more the ESV notes that supply is literally "staff".)

even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver but their own lives by their righteousness, declares the Lord GOD.

God names three men famous for their righteousness. Noah... was a righteous man, blameless in his generation (Gen 6:9). Job... was blameless and upright (Job 1:1). And Daniel — most naturally the Daniel of the book that bears his name, taken to Babylon as a young man years before (Dan 1:6) and already famous for wisdom (28:3). (Some readers have thought of an ancient figure of the same name, but the point does not change.)

Each of them was known for standing firm in a corrupt world. Noah saved his family through the flood. Job prayed for his children and his friends (Job 1:5; 42:8). Daniel stood faithful in a pagan court. Yet even they, God says, would save but their own lives.

That shatters a comfortable idea: that we can ride into God's favour on someone else's righteousness — a godly parent, a faithful church, a praying grandmother. Truly no man can ransom another, or give to God the price of his life (Ps 49:7). Each person must stand before God for himself.

verseByVerse.quote: "If I cause wild beasts to pass through the land, and they ravage it, and it be made desolate, so that no one may pass through because of the beasts, even if these three men were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters. They alone would be delivered, but the land would be desolate. "Or if I bring a sword upon that land and say, Let a sword pass through the land, and I cut off from it man and beast, though these three men were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they alone would be delivered. "Or if I send a pestilence into that land and pour out my wrath upon it with blood, to cut off from it man and beast, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would deliver neither son nor daughter. They would deliver but their own lives by their righteousness.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"If I cause wild beasts to pass through the land, and they ravage it, and it be made desolate, so that no one may pass through because of the beasts,

even if these three men were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters. They alone would be delivered, but the land would be desolate.

"Or if I bring a sword upon that land and say, Let a sword pass through the land, and I cut off from it man and beast,

though these three men were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they alone would be delivered.

"Or if I send a pestilence into that land and pour out my wrath upon it with blood, to cut off from it man and beast,

even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would deliver neither son nor daughter. They would deliver but their own lives by their righteousness.

Four times the same pattern, each with an oath: as I live. Wild beasts, sword, pestilence — and the same verdict. Neither sons nor daughters. This is especially striking because Noah's righteousness did save his family (Heb 11:7). But not here. Not in a land ripe for judgment.

That is a sobering word for parents. We long for our children to be saved, and we should pray and teach and live for that. But our faith cannot be credited to them. Each child must come to God personally.

And yet there is one righteousness that can be credited to others — only one. For as by the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners, so by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous (Rom 5:19). Noah, Daniel and Job could not save a single son or daughter. Jesus Christ saves everyone who trusts him: For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God (2 Cor 5:21). The gospel is exactly what this chapter says no human being could ever provide.

verseByVerse.quote: "For thus says the Lord GOD: How much more when I send upon Jerusalem my four disastrous acts of judgment, sword, famine, wild beasts, and pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast! But behold, some survivors will be left in it, sons and daughters who will be brought out; behold, when they come out to you, and you see their ways and their deeds, you will be consoled for the disaster that I have brought upon Jerusalem, for all that I have brought upon it. They will console you, when you see their ways and their deeds, and you shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
"For thus says the Lord GOD: How much more when I send upon Jerusalem my four disastrous acts of judgment, sword, famine, wild beasts, and pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast!

If one of those judgments would be beyond the power of three righteous men to avert, how much more all four together on Jerusalem.

These four — sword, famine, wild beasts and pestilence — are the covenant curses Moses listed (Lev 26:22-26), and they appear again at the end of the Bible, when the fourth horseman is given authority to kill with sword and with famine and with pestilence and by wild beasts of the earth (Rev 6:8). Jerusalem's fall was a preview of the judgment that will come on the whole world. The question Ezekiel 14 presses is the question of the last day: whose righteousness will you stand in?

But behold, some survivors will be left in it, sons and daughters who will be brought out; behold, when they come out to you, and you see their ways and their deeds, you will be consoled for the disaster that I have brought upon Jerusalem, for all that I have brought upon it.

They will console you, when you see their ways and their deeds, and you shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, declares the Lord GOD."

A surprising kind of consolation. Survivors will arrive in Babylon — not because they were righteous, but so that the exiles could see what they were like. And when the exiles see their ways and their deeds, they will understand. The destruction was not cruelty. I have not done without cause all that I have done.

There is real comfort in knowing that God's judgments are just. When we face disasters we cannot explain, we may not see the reasons. But we can rest on this: the Judge of all the earth does nothing without cause. One day every act of his will be seen to be right.

14.title: Idols in the Heart
14.overview:
Some elders of Israel come to consult Ezekiel. God reveals that they have taken idols into their hearts and asks whether he should let himself be consulted by them. Anyone who comes to a prophet while keeping idols in his heart will be answered by God himself, who wants to lay hold of hearts estranged from him. God calls the people to repent and turn from their idols. Whoever will not, whether Israelite or foreigner, God will set his face against and cut off; and a prophet who is deceived into speaking to such a person will share the same punishment, so that Israel will no longer stray but will be God's people (vv. 1-11).

God then declares that when a land sins faithlessly and he sends famine, wild beasts, sword or pestilence, even Noah, Daniel and Job could save only their own lives by their righteousness, not their sons or daughters. How much more when he sends all four judgments on Jerusalem. Yet some survivors will be brought out to the exiles, and when the exiles see their ways and deeds, they will be consoled, knowing that God did nothing in Jerusalem without cause (vv. 12-23).
14.theology:
Idolatry is first a matter of the heart; anything loved and trusted in God's place is an idol (vv. 3-4; Col 3:5; 1 John 5:21).

God will not be consulted by people who keep their idols, yet his confrontation aims to win back their hearts (vv. 3-5, 11).

Repentance means turning from idols and turning the face away from sin (v. 6); worship without it is in vain (Matt 15:8-9).

God may judicially give over those who love lies to the lies they want, without being the author of falsehood (vv. 9-10; 1 Kgs 22:20-23; 2 Thess 2:10-12; Titus 1:2).

No human righteousness can save another person, not even one's own children (vv. 14-20; Ps 49:7-8).

Only the righteousness of Christ is credited to others (Rom 5:19; 2 Cor 5:21).

God's judgments are never without cause (v. 23).
14.examples:
Elders asking God for guidance with idols tucked inside.

A stumbling block kept right in front of the face.

An answer that fits what you are carrying, not what you are saying.

Noah, Daniel and Job unable to save a single child.

The one righteousness that can be credited to someone else.

15.text: <sup>1</sup>And the word of the LORD came to me:<sup>2</sup>"Son of man, how does the wood of the vine surpass any wood, the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?<sup>3</sup>Is wood taken from it to make anything? Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on it?<sup>4</sup>Behold, it is given to the fire for fuel. When the fire has consumed both ends of it, and the middle of it is charred, is it useful for anything?<sup>5</sup>Behold, when it was whole, it was used for nothing. How much less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it ever be used for anything!<sup>6</sup>Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.<sup>7</sup>And I will set my face against them. Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them, and you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.<sup>8</sup>And I will make the land desolate, because they have acted faithlessly, declares the Lord GOD."

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–5 — Good for Nothing but Fruit
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God asks a simple question: how does the wood of the vine surpass any wood? (v. 2). You cannot make furniture from it, or even a peg to hang a pot on (v. 3). It is only fit for fuel, and once the fire has burned both ends and charred the middle, is it useful for anything? (v. 4). If it was useless whole, it is even more useless burned (v. 5).
verseByVerse.theology: A vine exists for fruit; without fruit it has no other use.

verseByVerse.quote: And the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, how does the wood of the vine surpass any wood, the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest? Is wood taken from it to make anything? Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on it?
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, how does the wood of the vine surpass any wood, the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?

A short chapter with one picture. Israel was proud to be God's vine. The psalm sang, You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out the nations and planted it (Ps 80:8). The exiles might have thought: surely God would never burn his own vine.

So God asks a question a child could answer. Compared with the timber of the forest — oak, cedar, cypress — what is so special about vine wood?

Is wood taken from it to make anything? Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on it?

The honest answer is: nothing. Vine wood is thin, twisted and weak. You cannot build a house with it, carve a tool from it, or even make a peg strong enough to hang a cooking pot. A vine has only one purpose — to bear grapes. Its glory is entirely in its fruit.

That was Israel's calling. God did not choose them because they were strong timber. He planted them to bear the fruit of justice, faithfulness and worship. Isaiah said, he looked for justice, but behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, but behold, an outcry! (Isa 5:7). Jeremiah: I planted you a choice vine... How then have you turned degenerate and become a wild vine? (Jer 2:21).

verseByVerse.quote: Behold, it is given to the fire for fuel. When the fire has consumed both ends of it, and the middle of it is charred, is it useful for anything? Behold, when it was whole, it was used for nothing. How much less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it ever be used for anything!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Behold, it is given to the fire for fuel. When the fire has consumed both ends of it, and the middle of it is charred, is it useful for anything?

Now think of a vine branch already thrown on the fire. Both ends are burned away; the middle is blackened. If it was useless before, what is it now?

One way to read the picture: both ends had already burned. The northern kingdom had been destroyed by Assyria, and the first deportation had taken Jehoiachin and the leaders of Jerusalem to Babylon. What remained in the middle was charred.

Behold, when it was whole, it was used for nothing. How much less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it ever be used for anything!

The logic is merciless. A fruitless vine is worthless whole; a fruitless, half-burned vine is worth even less. The people in Jerusalem thought that having survived the first deportation, they were the precious remnant (11:3). God says they are the charred middle of a stick.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem (v. 6). God will set his face against them; those who escape one fire will be caught by the next (v. 7), and the land will be desolate because they have acted faithlessly (v. 8).
verseByVerse.theology: God's people who bear no fruit have lost the only reason for their privileged place.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And I will set my face against them. Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them, and you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them. And I will make the land desolate, because they have acted faithlessly, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

The picture is decoded in one sentence. Jerusalem is the vine wood; the fire is God's judgment.

Religious privilege is not a shield. Being God's vine meant being expected to bear fruit. Jesus told a parable of a fig tree that bore nothing for three years: Cut it down. Why should it use up the ground? (Luke 13:7). And he warned the leaders of his day, the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people producing its fruits (Matt 21:43).

And I will set my face against them. Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them, and you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.

Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them. Those who survived 597 BC thought they had escaped. The fire of 586 was still to come.

And I will make the land desolate, because they have acted faithlessly, declares the Lord GOD."

The root of fruitlessness is unfaithfulness. A vine cut off from its source cannot bear fruit.

And that is exactly where Jesus takes this picture. Israel was the vine that failed. So he says, I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser (John 15:1). Christ is everything Israel was meant to be and was not. And then he speaks of us: I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing (John 15:5). The only way a branch bears fruit is by staying joined to him.

He uses Ezekiel's warning too: If anyone does not abide in me, he is thrown away like a branch and withers; and the branches are gathered, thrown into the fire, and burned (John 15:6). The fire of Ezekiel 15 is real. But the answer is not to try harder to be good timber. It is to abide in the true Vine, whose life flows into the branches and produces the fruit God is looking for.

15.title: The Wood of the Vine
15.overview:
God asks Ezekiel what makes the wood of a vine better than any tree of the forest. It cannot be used to make anything, not even a peg to hang a vessel on. It is fit only for fuel, and when the fire has burned both ends and charred the middle, it is useful for nothing. If it was useless when whole, it is even less useful when burned (vv. 1-5).

So God has given the people of Jerusalem to the fire, like vine wood. He will set his face against them; though they escape one fire, another will consume them, and they will know that he is the LORD. The land will be made desolate because they acted faithlessly (vv. 6-8).
15.theology:
God's people were planted to bear fruit, and their value lies there, not in any strength of their own (vv. 2-5; Ps 80:8-9; Isa 5:7; Jer 2:21).

Religious privilege without fruit is no protection from judgment (vv. 6-7; Luke 13:6-9; Matt 21:43).

Fruitlessness grows out of unfaithfulness (v. 8).

Christ is the true vine where Israel failed, and those who abide in him bear fruit; those who do not are gathered for the fire (John 15:1-6).
15.examples:
A stick too weak to hang a cooking pot on.

A branch burned at both ends, charred in the middle.

Surviving one fire and thinking you are safe.

The true Vine, and branches that cannot bear fruit on their own.

Were your whorings so small a matter<sup>21</sup>that you slaughtered my children and delivered them up as an offering by fire to them?<sup>22</sup>And in all your abominations and your whorings you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your blood.<sup>23</sup>"And after all your wickedness (woe, woe to you! declares the Lord GOD),<sup>24</sup>you built yourself a vaulted chamber and made yourself a lofty place in every square.<sup>25</sup>At the head of every street you built your lofty place and made your beauty an abomination, offering yourself to any passerby and multiplying your whoring.<sup>26</sup>You also played the whore with the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors, multiplying your whoring, to provoke me to anger.<sup>27</sup>Behold, therefore, I stretched out my hand against you and diminished your allotted portion and delivered you to the greed of your enemies, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd behavior.<sup>28</sup>You played the whore also with the Assyrians, because you were not satisfied; yes, you played the whore with them, and still you were not satisfied.<sup>29</sup>You multiplied your whoring also with the trading land of Chaldea, and even with this you were not satisfied.<sup>30</sup>"How sick is your heart, declares the Lord GOD, because you did all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute,<sup>31</sup>building your vaulted chamber at the head of every street, and making your lofty place in every square. I will gather them against you from every side and will uncover your nakedness to them, that they may see all your nakedness.<sup>38</sup>And I will judge you as women who commit adultery and shed blood are judged, and bring upon you the blood of wrath and jealousy.<sup>39</sup>And I will give you into their hands, and they shall throw down your vaulted chamber and break down your lofty places.
