Now you have become an object of reproach for the daughters of Syria and all those around her, and for the daughters of the Philistines, those all around who despise you.<sup>58</sup>You bear the penalty of your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.<sup>59</sup>"For thus says the Lord GOD: I will deal with you as you have done, you who have despised the oath in breaking the covenant,<sup>60</sup>yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant.<sup>61</sup>Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you take your sisters, both your elder and your younger, and I give them to you as daughters, but not on account of the covenant with you.<sup>62</sup>I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall know that I am the LORD,<sup>63</sup>that you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth again because of your shame, when I atone for you for all that you have done, declares the Lord GOD."

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–14 — Live! The Foundling Made a Queen
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Ezekiel must make Jerusalem know her abominations (v. 2). Her origins were pagan (v. 3). On the day she was born no one cut her cord, washed her or wrapped her; she was thrown into an open field, abhorred (vv. 4-5). Then God passed by and said to her, in your blood, 'Live!' (v. 6). She grew up (v. 7), and when she was of age he spread his garment over her, made his covenant with her, and you became mine (v. 8). He washed her, anointed her, clothed her in fine fabric and jewels and put a crown on her head (vv. 9-12), until she advanced to royalty and her fame spread, for it was perfect through the splendor that I had bestowed on you (vv. 13-14).
verseByVerse.theology: Everything God's people have — life, beauty, honour — is his undeserved gift to the helpless.

verseByVerse.quote: Again the word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations, and say, Thus says the Lord GOD to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth are of the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Again the word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations,

This is the longest chapter in Ezekiel, and it is meant to shock. God tells the story of Jerusalem as the story of a marriage: a baby girl abandoned at birth, rescued, raised, married and made a queen — who then betrays her husband with every passing stranger. The language is deliberately strong. God wants his people to feel what their idolatry is like from his side.

and say, Thus says the Lord GOD to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth are of the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.

The first blow is to Jerusalem's pride. The city was proud of its holy history. God says: your roots are pagan. Jerusalem had been a Canaanite city, held by the Jebusites until David took the stronghold of Zion (2 Sam 5:7).

The point is not ethnic but spiritual. There was nothing in Jerusalem's origins to make God choose her. Moses had told Israel the same: It was not because you were more in number than any other people that the LORD set his love on you... but it is because the LORD loves you (Deut 7:7-8). God's love does not find something lovely and choose it. It chooses, and then makes it lovely.

verseByVerse.quote: And as for your birth, on the day you were born your cord was not cut, nor were you washed with water to cleanse you, nor rubbed with salt, nor wrapped in swaddling cloths. No eye pitied you, to do any of these things to you out of compassion for you, but you were cast out on the open field, for you were abhorred, on the day that you were born.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And as for your birth, on the day you were born your cord was not cut, nor were you washed with water to cleanse you, nor rubbed with salt, nor wrapped in swaddling cloths.

Picture a newborn baby left exactly as she came into the world. No one has cut the umbilical cord. No one has washed her, rubbed her skin with salt as midwives did, or wrapped her in cloths to keep her warm. Every ordinary act of care has been refused.

No eye pitied you, to do any of these things to you out of compassion for you, but you were cast out on the open field, for you were abhorred, on the day that you were born.

And then she is thrown out into an open field to die. No eye pitied you. You were abhorred. In the ancient world, unwanted babies — often girls — were sometimes left out in exactly this way.

This is not only Jerusalem's story. It is ours. The Bible describes every human being by nature in the same terms: dead in the trespasses and sins, by nature children of wrath (Eph 2:1, 3). Helpless, unwanted, unable to do a single thing to save ourselves. That is where grace finds us. While we were still weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly (Rom 5:6).

verseByVerse.quote: "And when I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, I said to you in your blood, 'Live!' I said to you in your blood, 'Live!' I made you flourish like a plant of the field. And you grew up and became tall and arrived at full adornment. Your breasts were formed, and your hair had grown; yet you were naked and bare.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"And when I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, I said to you in your blood, 'Live!' I said to you in your blood, 'Live!'

Here is a great sentence of grace. I passed by you and saw you. Everyone else had passed by and looked away. God stops. And he does not wait until she is cleaned up. He speaks to her in your blood. Twice: Live!

That word does what it says. A baby cannot decide to live. God's command gives the life it commands. So it is with every believer: God, being rich in mercy, because of the great love with which he loved us, even when we were dead in our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ (Eph 2:4-5). Jesus said, the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live (John 5:25).

If you are a Christian, this is your story. You did not find God. He passed by, saw you in your blood, and said, Live.

I made you flourish like a plant of the field. And you grew up and became tall and arrived at full adornment. Your breasts were formed, and your hair had grown; yet you were naked and bare.

The rescued baby grows into a young woman under God's care. But she is still naked and bare — alive, but not yet clothed, not yet his bride. Life is only the beginning of what God intends.

verseByVerse.quote: "When I passed by you again and saw you, behold, you were at the age for love, and I spread the corner of my garment over you and covered your nakedness; I made my vow to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord GOD, and you became mine.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"When I passed by you again and saw you, behold, you were at the age for love, and I spread the corner of my garment over you and covered your nakedness; I made my vow to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord GOD, and you became mine.

I passed by you again. The second passing is not rescue but romance. You were at the age for love.

I spread the corner of my garment over you. This was a gesture of marriage. Ruth asked Boaz to do exactly this: Spread your wings over your servant, for you are a redeemer (Ruth 3:9). It meant protection, provision and belonging.

Then I made my vow to you and entered into a covenant with you. This is Sinai, where God bound himself to Israel: you shall be my treasured possession among all peoples (Exod 19:5). And the most beautiful words in the verse are the last: and you became mine.

God does not just rescue people and leave them. He takes them as his own. The whole Bible is the story of a marriage — from God's covenant with Israel to the marriage of the Lamb (Rev 19:7). Paul says of the church, I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ (2 Cor 11:2).

verseByVerse.quote: Then I bathed you with water and washed off your blood from you and anointed you with oil. I clothed you also with embroidered cloth and shod you with fine leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk. And I adorned you with ornaments and put bracelets on your wrists and a chain on your neck. And I put a ring on your nose and earrings in your ears and a beautiful crown on your head.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then I bathed you with water and washed off your blood from you and anointed you with oil.

Now the husband does what no one did at her birth: he washes her, cleans off the blood, and anoints her with oil. Everything that was neglected, he supplies.

This is what Christ does for his bride: he gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word, so that he might present the church to himself in splendor, without spot or wrinkle (Eph 5:25-27).

I clothed you also with embroidered cloth and shod you with fine leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk.

And I adorned you with ornaments and put bracelets on your wrists and a chain on your neck.

And I put a ring on your nose and earrings in your ears and a beautiful crown on your head.

Embroidered cloth (the ESV notes, "rich fabric"), fine leather sandals, linen, silk, bracelets, a necklace, a nose ring, earrings, a crown. Everything a queen would wear. The girl from the field is dressed as royalty.

And every piece is a gift. She bought none of it. That is exactly how the gospel describes salvation: he has clothed me with the garments of salvation; he has covered me with the robe of righteousness (Isa 61:10). Like the returning prodigal, given the best robe and a ring on his hand (Luke 15:22), the bride wears what her husband gave.

verseByVerse.quote: Thus you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was of fine linen and silk and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour and honey and oil. You grew exceedingly beautiful and advanced to royalty. And your renown went forth among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect through the splendor that I had bestowed on you, declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Thus you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was of fine linen and silk and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour and honey and oil. You grew exceedingly beautiful and advanced to royalty.

Fine flour, honey, oil — the best food. You... advanced to royalty: this is the kingdom of David and Solomon, when Jerusalem became a royal city with a temple of gold.

And your renown went forth among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect through the splendor that I had bestowed on you, declares the Lord GOD.

The nations talked about Jerusalem. The Queen of Sheba came to see (1 Kgs 10:1). But look at the last phrase: perfect through the splendor that I had bestowed on you. Her beauty was real, and it was borrowed. All of it came from him.

Here is the question the rest of the chapter turns on. What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it? (1 Cor 4:7). The moment we forget that our gifts are gifts, we are ready to use them against the Giver.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 15–34 — You Trusted in Your Beauty
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: But you trusted in your beauty and played the whore (v. 15). She turned God's gifts — garments, gold, oil, incense, bread — into shrines and idols (vv. 16-19). She sacrificed the children she had borne to God (vv. 20-21), forgetting the days when she lay in her blood (v. 22). She built shrines in every square (vv. 23-25) and ran after Egypt, Assyria and Babylon, never satisfied (vv. 26-29). She was worse than a prostitute: she paid her lovers (vv. 30-34).
verseByVerse.theology: Unfaithfulness to God begins when his gifts are trusted instead of the Giver, and it never satisfies.

verseByVerse.quote: "But you trusted in your beauty and played the whore because of your renown and lavished your whorings on any passerby; your beauty became his. You took some of your garments and made for yourself colorful shrines, and on them played the whore. The like has never been, nor ever shall be.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"But you trusted in your beauty and played the whore because of your renown and lavished your whorings on any passerby; your beauty became his.

But. After all that grace, one word turns the story. You trusted in your beauty. That is where it began: not with an obvious sin, but with trusting the gift instead of the Giver.

The ESV notes that played the whore may also be rendered "were unfaithful", and whorings "unfaithfulness". The language is shocking on purpose. Idolatry is not a harmless religious preference. It is adultery against a husband who rescued you from death. James uses the same word for Christians who love the world: You adulterous people! (Jas 4:4).

Lavished your whorings on any passerby; your beauty became his. The beauty God gave her she gave away to strangers. Every idol Israel worshipped was paid for with God's gifts.

You took some of your garments and made for yourself colorful shrines, and on them played the whore. The like has never been, nor ever shall be.

The clothes her husband gave her she cut up to decorate pagan shrines. (The ESV notes that the meaning of the last sentence is uncertain.) The picture is of taking the very gifts of grace and turning them into the furnishings of idolatry.

verseByVerse.quote: You also took your beautiful jewels of my gold and of my silver, which I had given you, and made for yourself images of men, and with them played the whore. And you took your embroidered garments to cover them, and set my oil and my incense before them. Also my bread that I gave you— I fed you with fine flour and oil and honey—you set before them for a pleasing aroma; and so it was, declares the Lord GOD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
You also took your beautiful jewels of my gold and of my silver, which I had given you, and made for yourself images of men, and with them played the whore.

And you took your embroidered garments to cover them, and set my oil and my incense before them.

Also my bread that I gave you— I fed you with fine flour and oil and honey—you set before them for a pleasing aroma; and so it was, declares the Lord GOD.

Listen to the repeated word: my. My gold, my silver, my oil, my incense, my bread. God keeps pointing out whose gifts they were. Hosea said the same: she did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the wine, and the oil, and who lavished on her silver and gold, which they used for Baal (Hos 2:8).

Imagine a wife taking the jewellery her husband gave her, melting it down to make statues of other men, dressing them in the clothes he bought, and feeding them the meals from his table. That is idolatry.

And it is not only ancient. Every gift God gives can be turned into an idol — money, sexuality, intelligence, beauty, family, even ministry. The test is simple: am I using this to love and serve God, or am I using it to love and serve something in his place?

verseByVerse.quote: And you took your sons and your daughters, whom you had borne to me, and these you sacrificed to them to be devoured. Were your whorings so small a matter that you slaughtered my children and delivered them up as an offering by fire to them? And in all your abominations and your whorings you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your blood.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And you took your sons and your daughters, whom you had borne to me, and these you sacrificed to them to be devoured. Were your whorings so small a matter

that you slaughtered my children and delivered them up as an offering by fire to them?

Now the worst. Judah's kings had actually burned their children as offerings. Ahaz even burned his son as an offering (2 Kgs 16:3), and so did Manasseh (2 Kgs 21:6). In the Valley of Hinnom they built altars to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which I did not command, nor did it come into my mind (Jer 7:31).

And God says: my children. The children were his. They had been borne to me. Idolatry always ends up sacrificing the next generation. Cultures that worship pleasure, success or self still sacrifice children on those altars, sometimes literally, often in quieter ways.

And in all your abominations and your whorings you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your blood.

Here is the root of it all: you did not remember. She forgot where she came from — the field, the blood, the voice that said Live. Moses had warned: when you have eaten and are full and have built good houses... then your heart be lifted up, and you forget the LORD your God (Deut 8:12, 14).

The cure for unfaithfulness is remembering grace. Christians gather around the Lord's Table for exactly this reason: to remember.

verseByVerse.quote: "And after all your wickedness (woe, woe to you! declares the Lord GOD), you built yourself a vaulted chamber and made yourself a lofty place in every square. At the head of every street you built your lofty place and made your beauty an abomination, offering yourself to any passerby and multiplying your whoring.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"And after all your wickedness (woe, woe to you! declares the Lord GOD),

you built yourself a vaulted chamber and made yourself a lofty place in every square.

At the head of every street you built your lofty place and made your beauty an abomination, offering yourself to any passerby and multiplying your whoring.

The idolatry is no longer hidden. Shrines stand in every square and at the head of every street. What once would have been done in secret is now done in public, without shame.

That is how sin progresses. First it is hidden (8:12). Then it is tolerated. Then it is celebrated on every street corner. God's cry in the middle — woe, woe to you! — is a cry of grief as well as judgment.

verseByVerse.quote: You also played the whore with the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors, multiplying your whoring, to provoke me to anger. Behold, therefore, I stretched out my hand against you and diminished your allotted portion and delivered you to the greed of your enemies, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd behavior. You played the whore also with the Assyrians, because you were not satisfied; yes, you played the whore with them, and still you were not satisfied. You multiplied your whoring also with the trading land of Chaldea, and even with this you were not satisfied.
verseByVerse.commentary:
You also played the whore with the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors, multiplying your whoring, to provoke me to anger.

Now the unfaithfulness turns political. Judah's alliances with foreign powers are called adultery too. Egypt, Assyria, Babylon — each time, instead of trusting God, Judah ran to a superpower for protection, and took on its gods as part of the deal.

Behold, therefore, I stretched out my hand against you and diminished your allotted portion and delivered you to the greed of your enemies, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd behavior.

Even the pagan Philistines were ashamed of your lewd behavior. When God's people behave worse than the world, the world notices.

You played the whore also with the Assyrians, because you were not satisfied; yes, you played the whore with them, and still you were not satisfied.

You multiplied your whoring also with the trading land of Chaldea, and even with this you were not satisfied.

Three times: not satisfied. That is the nature of every idol. It promises fulfilment and leaves you hungrier. Each new lover is a little more exciting and a little less satisfying.

Jesus said at a well to a woman who had had five husbands, Everyone who drinks of this water will be thirsty again, but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never be thirsty again (John 4:13-14). Only the true Husband satisfies.

verseByVerse.quote: "How sick is your heart, declares the Lord GOD, because you did all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute, building your vaulted chamber at the head of every street, and making your lofty place in every square. Yet you were not like a prostitute, because you scorned payment. Adulterous wife, who receives strangers instead of her husband! Men give gifts to all prostitutes, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, bribing them to come to you from every side with your whorings. So you were different from other women in your whorings. No one solicited you to play the whore, and you gave payment, while no payment was given to you; therefore you were different.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"How sick is your heart, declares the Lord GOD, because you did all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute,

How sick is your heart. (The ESV notes that another vocalization gives "How I am filled with anger against you".) Either way, the diagnosis goes to the heart.

building your vaulted chamber at the head of every street, and making your lofty place in every square. Yet you were not like a prostitute, because you scorned payment.

Adulterous wife, who receives strangers instead of her husband!

Men give gifts to all prostitutes, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, bribing them to come to you from every side with your whorings.

So you were different from other women in your whorings. No one solicited you to play the whore, and you gave payment, while no payment was given to you; therefore you were different.

Here is a humiliating twist. A prostitute at least gets paid. Jerusalem paid her lovers. She sent tribute to Egypt and Assyria, bribing them to come. Ephraim has hired lovers, Hosea said (Hos 8:9).

That is what idolatry does. It makes us pay for our own ruin. We spend money, time, health and relationships on things that give us nothing back.

And set it against the gospel. God's people paid their lovers. God paid for his bride. Hosea was told to buy back his unfaithful wife: So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver (Hos 3:2). And Christ bought his church at an infinitely higher price, with the precious blood of Christ (1 Pet 1:19).

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Because of her unfaithfulness and the blood of her children (vv. 35-36), God will gather her lovers against her and expose her (v. 37). She will be judged as an adulteress and murderer (v. 38): stripped, stoned, cut down, her houses burned (vv. 39-41). Then God's wrath will be satisfied and he will be calm (v. 42), Because you have not remembered the days of your youth (v. 43).
verseByVerse.theology: God's jealous love will not overlook covenant betrayal; the very powers she courted become the instruments of her judgment.

verseByVerse.quote: "Therefore, O prostitute, hear the word of the LORD: Thus says the Lord GOD, Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness uncovered in your whorings with your lovers, and with all your abominable idols, and because of the blood of your children that you gave to them, therefore, behold, I will gather all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from every side and will uncover your nakedness to them, that they may see all your nakedness. And I will judge you as women who commit adultery and shed blood are judged, and bring upon you the blood of wrath and jealousy.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Therefore, O prostitute, hear the word of the LORD:

Thus says the Lord GOD, Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness uncovered in your whorings with your lovers, and with all your abominable idols, and because of the blood of your children that you gave to them,

The charges are summed up: unfaithfulness, idols, and the blood of your children.

therefore, behold, I will gather all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from every side and will uncover your nakedness to them, that they may see all your nakedness.

The judgment fits the sin exactly. The nations she courted will be gathered against her. Babylon, whom she invited in, will be the army at her walls. Her shame, which she displayed to them, will be exposed by them. The things we run to instead of God often become the very things that turn on us.

And I will judge you as women who commit adultery and shed blood are judged, and bring upon you the blood of wrath and jealousy.

Under the law, adultery and murder were capital crimes (Lev 20:10). Jerusalem was guilty of both. And the judgment comes with jealousy — the burning anger of a wronged husband. God's wrath is not cold. It is the wrath of betrayed love.

verseByVerse.quote: And I will give you into their hands, and they shall throw down your vaulted chamber and break down your lofty places. They shall strip you of your clothes and take your beautiful jewels and leave you naked and bare. They shall bring up a crowd against you, and they shall stone you and cut you to pieces with their swords. And they shall burn your houses and execute judgments upon you in the sight of many women. I will make you stop playing the whore, and you shall also give payment no more.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And I will give you into their hands, and they shall throw down your vaulted chamber and break down your lofty places. They shall strip you of your clothes and take your beautiful jewels and leave you naked and bare.

Everything God gave is taken back. The clothes, the jewels — gone. And she is left naked and bare, exactly the words used of her as a girl before God covered her (v. 7). Grace despised leaves a person where grace found them.

They shall bring up a crowd against you, and they shall stone you and cut you to pieces with their swords.

And they shall burn your houses and execute judgments upon you in the sight of many women. I will make you stop playing the whore, and you shall also give payment no more.

The picture of an adulteress stoned becomes the reality of a city besieged, broken and burned. In the sight of many women — in front of all the nations. And it will stop. The idolatry will end, because the city that practised it will be gone.

verseByVerse.quote: So will I satisfy my wrath on you, and my jealousy shall depart from you. I will be calm and will no more be angry. Because you have not remembered the days of your youth, but have enraged me with all these things, therefore, behold, I have returned your deeds upon your head, declares the Lord GOD. Have you not committed lewdness in addition to all your abominations?
verseByVerse.commentary:
So will I satisfy my wrath on you, and my jealousy shall depart from you. I will be calm and will no more be angry.

I will be calm and will no more be angry. God's anger is real, and it has an end. When justice has been done, it is satisfied.

That is the heart of the gospel. God's wrath against the sin of his people did not simply fade away. It was satisfied — not on them, but on Christ, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood (Rom 3:25). And so God can say to his people, as he said through Isaiah, I have sworn that I will not be angry with you, and will not rebuke you (Isa 54:9).

Because you have not remembered the days of your youth, but have enraged me with all these things, therefore, behold, I have returned your deeds upon your head, declares the Lord GOD. Have you not committed lewdness in addition to all your abominations?

Once more: you have not remembered the days of your youth. Forgetfulness is named as the root of it all a second time. The best defence against drifting from God is a daily, grateful memory of what he has done.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: People will say of Jerusalem, Like mother, like daughter (vv. 44-45). Her sisters are Samaria and Sodom (v. 46), and she has become more corrupt than both (v. 47). Behold, this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy (vv. 48-50). Jerusalem has made her sisters look righteous (vv. 51-52). Yet God will restore the fortunes of Sodom, Samaria and Jerusalem together, to Jerusalem's shame (vv. 53-55). The city that once sneered at Sodom now bears the scorn of her neighbours (vv. 56-58).
verseByVerse.theology: The self-righteous who despise notorious sinners may be more guilty than they, and God's mercy reaches farther than they imagine.

verseByVerse.quote: "Behold, everyone who uses proverbs will use this proverb about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.' You are the daughter of your mother, who loathed her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite. And your elder sister is Samaria, who lived with her daughters to the north of you; and your younger sister, who lived to the south of you, is Sodom with her daughters. Not only did you walk in their ways and do according to their abominations; within a very little time you were more corrupt than they in all your ways.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"Behold, everyone who uses proverbs will use this proverb about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.'

You are the daughter of your mother, who loathed her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.

A new picture. Jerusalem has become exactly like the pagan family she came from — a mother who hated her husband and children. For all God's grace, she went back to her roots.

And your elder sister is Samaria, who lived with her daughters to the north of you; and your younger sister, who lived to the south of you, is Sodom with her daughters.

Two sisters. Samaria, capital of the northern kingdom, destroyed by Assyria for its idolatry. And Sodom, the byword for wickedness, destroyed by fire. The people of Jerusalem looked down on both.

Not only did you walk in their ways and do according to their abominations; within a very little time you were more corrupt than they in all your ways.

And God says: you are worse than both, and it did not take you long.

verseByVerse.quote: As I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done. Behold, this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy. They were haughty and did an abomination before me. So I removed them, when I saw it.
verseByVerse.commentary:
As I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done.

With an oath God declares that Sodom was not as bad as Jerusalem. That would have stunned every hearer. Why? Because Jerusalem had the law, the temple, the prophets and the covenant, and sinned anyway. The more light you have, the darker your sin.

Behold, this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy.

They were haughty and did an abomination before me. So I removed them, when I saw it.

Here is a description of Sodom's sin that many people have never noticed. Pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy. And alongside it, They were haughty and did an abomination. Genesis records the men of Sodom surrounding Lot's house to abuse his guests (Gen 19:4-5), and Jude says they indulged in sexual immorality and pursued unnatural desire (Jude 7). Scripture holds both together: the sexual abomination and the proud, comfortable neglect of the poor. We must not use either to hide from the other.

This is a searching word for prosperous societies and prosperous churches. Pride. Too much food. Comfortable ease. Indifference to the needy. Amos pictured the same people: Woe to those who lie on beds of ivory... but are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph! (Amos 6:4, 6). Paul told Timothy to charge the rich not to be haughty but to be generous and ready to share (1 Tim 6:17-18). Before we condemn Sodom, we should ask whether its description fits us.

verseByVerse.quote: Samaria has not committed half your sins. You have committed more abominations than they, and have made your sisters appear righteous by all the abominations that you have committed. Bear your disgrace, you also, for you have intervened on behalf of your sisters. Because of your sins in which you acted more abominably than they, they are more in the right than you. So be ashamed, you also, and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters appear righteous.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Samaria has not committed half your sins. You have committed more abominations than they, and have made your sisters appear righteous by all the abominations that you have committed.

Made your sisters appear righteous. Next to Jerusalem, Samaria and Sodom look good. That is a devastating reversal for a people who defined themselves by being better than others.

Bear your disgrace, you also, for you have intervened on behalf of your sisters. Because of your sins in which you acted more abominably than they, they are more in the right than you. So be ashamed, you also, and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters appear righteous.

Twice in one verse: bear your disgrace. Jerusalem must accept her shame instead of pointing at others.

Religious people are always tempted to measure themselves against the worst sinners they can find. The Pharisee prayed, God, I thank you that I am not like other men (Luke 18:11). Paul says, in passing judgment on another you condemn yourself, because you, the judge, practice the very same things (Rom 2:1). The measure is not other people. It is God.

verseByVerse.quote: "I will restore their fortunes, both the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters, and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and I will restore your own fortunes in their midst, that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all that you have done, becoming a consolation to them. As for your sisters, Sodom and her daughters shall return to their former state, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former state, and you and your daughters shall return to your former state.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"I will restore their fortunes, both the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters, and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and I will restore your own fortunes in their midst,

And now something no one could have expected. God will restore — not only Jerusalem, but Sodom and Samaria too. The destroyed city and the fallen northern kingdom are included in the promise of mercy.

that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all that you have done, becoming a consolation to them.

Notice where Jerusalem is placed: in their midst. Not above them, but among them. When God restores her, it will not be as the superior sister but as one sinner among others, humbled and shamed, receiving the same mercy.

As for your sisters, Sodom and her daughters shall return to their former state, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former state, and you and your daughters shall return to your former state.

How this will be fulfilled is not spelled out. But the direction is clear: God's mercy reaches farther than Jerusalem's pride could imagine — to the despised and the destroyed. The New Testament gives a foretaste when Samaria had received the word of God (Acts 8:14), and when the gospel went out to the nations. The people Jerusalem despised were welcomed into the same mercy.

verseByVerse.quote: Was not your sister Sodom a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride, before your wickedness was uncovered? Now you have become an object of reproach for the daughters of Syria and all those around her, and for the daughters of the Philistines, those all around who despise you. You bear the penalty of your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Was not your sister Sodom a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride,

before your wickedness was uncovered? Now you have become an object of reproach for the daughters of Syria and all those around her, and for the daughters of the Philistines, those all around who despise you.

Jerusalem used to say "Sodom" as a byword, a joke, an insult — in the day of your pride. Now her own wickedness has been uncovered, and the neighbours mock her. (The ESV notes that some manuscripts read "of Edom" for of Syria.)

The people we sneer at in our pride may one day be the ones who see our own exposure. Humility is always safer than contempt.

You bear the penalty of your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God will deal with Jerusalem as she deserves for breaking the covenant (v. 59), yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant (v. 60). She will remember and be ashamed when God gives her sisters to her as daughters (v. 61). He will establish his covenant (v. 62), that you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth again because of your shame, when I atone for you for all that you have done (v. 63).
verseByVerse.theology: Where the bride failed completely, the Husband keeps the covenant and makes atonement himself.

verseByVerse.quote: "For thus says the Lord GOD: I will deal with you as you have done, you who have despised the oath in breaking the covenant, yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant.
verseByVerse.commentary:
"For thus says the Lord GOD: I will deal with you as you have done, you who have despised the oath in breaking the covenant,

Justice first. She despised the oath. She broke the covenant. God will deal with her accordingly.

yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant.

Yet. Here is the turn of the whole chapter. Twice Jerusalem did not remember the days of her youth (vv. 22, 43). Now God says, I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth. She forgot; he remembers. Her faithfulness failed; his does not.

And he will do more than restore the old covenant. I will establish for you an everlasting covenant — one that cannot be broken because it does not depend on her. Jeremiah heard the same promise: I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from doing good to them. And I will put the fear of me in their hearts, that they may not turn from me (Jer 32:40).

That covenant was sealed on the night Jesus said, This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood (Luke 22:20), and the God of peace... brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus... by the blood of the eternal covenant (Heb 13:20).

verseByVerse.quote: Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you take your sisters, both your elder and your younger, and I give them to you as daughters, but not on account of the covenant with you. I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall know that I am the LORD, that you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth again because of your shame, when I atone for you for all that you have done, declares the Lord GOD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you take your sisters, both your elder and your younger, and I give them to you as daughters, but not on account of the covenant with you.

When grace comes, memory finally works. Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed. Not the shame of being caught, but the healthy shame of seeing clearly what you were and what God has done.

And the sisters she despised will be given to her as daughters — brought into the family of God through her. (The ESV notes that the last phrase may be read "not apart from the covenant with you".) The despised become family.

I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall know that I am the LORD,

that you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth again because of your shame, when I atone for you for all that you have done, declares the Lord GOD."

Here is the last line of this long, dark chapter, and it is pure gospel: when I atone for you for all that you have done. Not when you atone. When I atone. The husband pays for the adultery of the bride.

And the result is silence: never open your mouth again because of your shame. Not a silence of despair, but of wonder. There is nothing left to say — no excuses, no boasting, no comparing yourself with others. Every mouth may be stopped before God (Rom 3:19), and every sinner who is saved is saved by grace... not a result of works, so that no one may boast (Eph 2:8-9).

That is where Ezekiel 16 leaves us: a foundling picked up out of her blood, a queen who betrayed her rescuer, and a husband who, instead of divorcing her, makes atonement for her himself. The story ends where the Bible ends: the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband (Rev 21:2).

16.title: The Foundling Bride
16.overview:
God tells Jerusalem's story as the story of a marriage. She was born of pagan stock and abandoned at birth in an open field, uncared for and despised. God passed by, saw her in her blood and said, Live. She grew up, and when she was of age he spread his garment over her, made a covenant with her, and she became his. He washed and anointed her, dressed her in fine clothes and jewels, crowned her, fed her with the best food, and she became a queen whose beauty was famous among the nations — a beauty that was his gift (vv. 1-14).

But she trusted in her beauty and was unfaithful. She used God's gifts of clothing, gold, oil, incense and bread to make and serve idols, sacrificed her children to them, and forgot the days when she lay in her blood. She built shrines in every square and ran after Egypt, Assyria and Babylon, never satisfied, and was worse than a prostitute because she paid her lovers (vv. 15-34).

So God will gather her lovers against her, expose her, and judge her as an adulteress and murderer: stripped, stoned and burned, until his wrath is satisfied, because she did not remember the days of her youth (vv. 35-43). Like her pagan mother, she has become worse than her sisters Samaria and Sodom, whose guilt was pride, excess, ease, neglect of the poor and abomination. Yet God will restore the fortunes of Sodom, Samaria and Jerusalem, to Jerusalem's shame (vv. 44-58).

God will deal with her as she deserves, yet he will remember his covenant from her youth and establish an everlasting covenant. She will remember and be ashamed, receive her sisters as daughters, and never open her mouth again because of her shame when God atones for all she has done (vv. 59-63).
16.theology:
God's love is sovereign and undeserved: he chooses and gives life to the helpless and unlovely (vv. 3-8; Deut 7:7-8; Eph 2:1-5).

Everything God's people have is his gift; beauty and honour are bestowed, not earned (vv. 9-14; 1 Cor 4:7).

Idolatry is spiritual adultery; it begins with trusting the gifts instead of the Giver, uses God's gifts for other gods, and never satisfies (vv. 15-34; Hos 2:8; Jas 4:4; John 4:13-14).

Forgetting grace is the root of unfaithfulness (vv. 22, 43; Deut 8:11-14).

Greater privilege brings greater guilt; the proud who despise notorious sinners may be worse than they (vv. 47-52; Luke 18:11; Rom 2:1).

Sodom's sin included both sexual abomination and proud, comfortable neglect of the poor (vv. 49-50; Gen 19:4-5; Jude 7).

God's wrath is real and is satisfied; in Christ it was satisfied for his people (v. 42; Rom 3:25).

Where the bride failed, the husband remembers his covenant, establishes an everlasting covenant and makes atonement himself, silencing all boasting (vv. 60-63; Jer 32:40; Luke 22:20; Heb 13:20; Rom 3:19; Eph 2:8-9).

Christ is the Bridegroom who cleanses, clothes and presents his bride (Eph 5:25-27; Rev 19:7-8; 21:2).
16.examples:
A newborn left in a field with the cord still uncut.

A voice that says Live to a baby in her blood.

A cloak spread over a young woman: you are mine.

A queen melting down her wedding jewellery to make statues of other men.

Paying your lovers to use you.

Pride, full stomachs, easy lives and closed hands.

Next to you, even Sodom looks righteous.

A husband who, instead of divorcing, atones.

A mouth that never opens again, except in wonder.
